correctness.rationale: A nonclique triple necessarily repeats a row or column. Coordinate relabeling leaves exactly three cases, with explicit induced paths (00,11,02,10,01), (00,21,10,01), and (00,12,01); their nonconsecutive vertices share a coordinate, so all three witnesses are chordless. The third selected vertex is internal for each repeated-coordinate pair. Conversely, an induced path cannot contain three clique vertices. Injection of chosen rows into distinct columns counts all cliques; nonadjacent pairs cannot extend and all smaller cliques can. Boundary p,q=3 supplies every necessary fresh coordinate. Independent direct adjacency and DFS induced-path enumeration gave forbidden triples exactly equal to all nonclique triples for 3x3 (78) and 3x4 (196), and the claimed counts for small boards. These tests are corroboration; the canonical witness argument proves the unrestricted family.
residual_risks: The proof relies on the completeness of the three repeated-coordinate equality cases; classification deliberately excludes two-row/factor-two boundaries.
Finite tests do not establish all p,q.

originality.rationale: The closest monophonic-position theorem of Thomas–Chandran–Tuite–Di Stefano gives a general induced disjoint-union-of-cliques constraint, not a clique-only rule for categorical products. Later monophonic-product work concerns Cartesian or lexicographic products; results about K_p×K_q in geodesic general position count different feasible sets. Brešar–Cornet–Dravec formulate strongly 2-monophonic coverage, but their relevant Hamming examples are Cartesian rather than categorical products. The new exact induced-path witnesses supply the classification and inclusion-maximal enumerator. This is best-of-knowledge, not proof of absolute priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed monophonic-position theorem for the complement of a rook graph could provide equivalent coverage.
A stronger published graph-interval condition might imply the classification by specialization.

value.rationale: A complete finite-set enumerator and inclusion-maximality spectrum for every categorical product K_p×K_q resolves a natural induced-path graph invariant. The strongly-2-monophonic conclusion constructs an additional vertex-transitive diameter-two family, while the gap between lower and upper maximal sizes and the contrast with geodesic general position become arbitrarily large; these are structural rather than isolated computations.
